title: How we pack a mug so it gets there in one piece
excerpt: Paper, card and a shake test. In ten years we've sent twelve thousand pieces, and broken fewer than one in five hundred.
content:
Every order is packed by Ellie, by hand, in the mornings. Here's how.

Paper, not plastic

Each piece is wrapped in two layers of paper and stood in a nest of shredded card.

The shake test

Before a box is taped, Ellie shakes it. If anything moves, it gets more card.

If it breaks anyway

Send us a photo and we'll send another. It happens rarely, but it happens.

title: Caring for stoneware: the dishwasher, the oven and the odd grey mark
excerpt: Our pieces are made for every day. A few small habits keep them looking new for years.
content:
Stoneware is tough, but it isn't magic. These are the questions we're asked most.

The dishwasher

Fine, every day. The glaze is fired to 2,300°F and won't fade.

The oven

A warm oven is fine. Avoid going straight from the fridge into a hot oven.

Grey marks

Knives can leave grey lines on plates. A paste of baking soda and water takes them off.

title: A day at the wheel
excerpt: Forty mugs before lunch, handles after, and the kiln on overnight. What a making day in the studio looks like.
content:
Tuesdays and Thursdays are making days. Here's how one goes.

Morning

June wedges the clay and throws, usually forty mugs or twenty bowls before lunch.

Afternoon

Yesterday's pieces are leather hard, so they're trimmed and get their handles.

Night

Marcus loads the kiln. It runs for twelve hours and cools for a day.

title: Saturday mornings at the studio
excerpt: Come and watch us throw, have a go on the wheel and take home what you make once it's fired.
content:
Every Saturday from 10am the wheel is open to visitors.

Watch

June throws for an hour and answers questions.

Have a go

Two wheels are free for anyone who'd like to try. Aprons provided.

Take it home

We fire what you make and you can collect it two weeks later, or we'll ship it.
